podcast.title: Band Name Choice
podcast.body: This was one of Kurt Cobain's first bands, and its name, Fecal Matter, highlights his pervasive curiosity about and obsession with human excretia and bodily functions. "Remember this is a man who named one of his first bands Fiko Matter."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Band Name History – From Fecal Matter to Ed Ted Fred to Nirvana (March 19, 1988)
xref.body: Kurt's first band was called Fecal Matter (fall 1985). Subsequent incarnations included Brown Towel (sometimes misbilled as Brown Cow). The first Kurt-and-Krist performance was at a house party on March 7, 1987, as "Skid Row" (unrelated to the metal band), with drummer Aaron Burkhard. Names considered at the time included Batguano, Designer Drugs, Gut Bomb, Egg Flog, Fish Food, Puking Worms, Bliss, Whiskey Biscuit, Incompetent Fools, Poo Poo Box, Pen Cap Chew, Throat Oyster, Window Frame, Yin-Yang Valvstem, and Ed Ted Fred. They entered the studio on January 2, 1988, still as "Ed Ted Fred." The name Nirvana was first used at a show in Tacoma on March 19, 1988 — Kurt was studying Buddhism and liked that Nirvana meant a state free from pain, worry, and the troubles of the world, reflecting his ongoing stomach problems and the psychological damage of his parents' divorce. "He was dabbling in Buddhism at the time and learned that Nirvana meant a state or place that was free from pain, worry, and the troubles of the world."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Fascination with Human Excretia
xref.body: Cobain demonstrated a strong curiosity about various types of human excretia, including vomit, urine, mucus, and poop. This interest was so pronounced that he named one of his early bands "Fecal Matter." "Kurt also created things like weird landscapes filled with images like diseased vaginas. There's just no other way to say it."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Medical Fetish – Anatomy Art, Gynecological Instruments, Full-Sized Medical Dummy on Tour
xref.body: Kurt Cobain's artistic aesthetic included a deep preoccupation with medical imagery and human anatomy that dated back to his grade school drawings. The artwork for *In Utero* features disassembled dolls, fetuses, and embryo-like forms. He reportedly collected vintage medical equipment and surgical instruments, including old gynecological devices well beyond basic medical tools. One account claims he kept a full-sized medical dummy at home and took it on tour in its own trunk. His journals (published by Courtney Love in 2002) reveal an obsession with bodily functions, vomit, urine, mucus, and excrement — consistent with his naming of his first band Fecal Matter. "Kurt had a full-sized medical dummy. Not only did he keep it around the house, but he toured with it."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
